lesson_activities.title: A new tool is not yet a new habit

activity.prompt: Which success statement is most observable for Cedar Service?

options.text: People are excited about transformation.
options.feedback: This may matter, but it does not specify a work behavior you can inspect.

options.text: Everyone received a launch email.
options.feedback: Message delivery is an activity, not evidence of the new handoff behavior.

options.text: At shift end, each open ticket has an owner and a recorded next action.
options.feedback: Best choice. It identifies the action, setting and evidence.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which element concerns carrying out new skills in practice?

options.text: Awareness
Ability
Reinforcement

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Ability concerns demonstrated performance. Hearing about a process or recalling it is different evidence.

lesson_activities.title: Explore purpose and concerns

activity.prompt: Priya raises the ranking concern. What do you say first?

options.text: “You just need the tutorial again.”
options.feedback: A tutorial addresses steps, not the stated concern. Priya may feel unheard.

options.text: “What use of the ticket data concerns you? Let’s check the actual policy before I answer.”
options.feedback: Best choice. You listen, identify the issue and avoid an unsupported promise.

options.text: “Nobody will ever use those numbers for evaluation.”
options.feedback: This assurance could be false. Verify policy and communicate honestly.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Alex cannot explain why the handoff is changing. What is the earliest likely support need?

options.text: Explain the reason and check understanding
Schedule a reward ceremony
Assign an advanced keyboard-shortcut exercise

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The stated evidence points to a purpose gap. Address that before assuming later-stage support is the main need.

lesson_activities.title: Separate knowing from doing

activity.prompt: Nia explains the steps correctly but her account cannot assign tickets. Choose the most useful immediate response.

options.text: Repeat the same explanation more slowly.
options.feedback: The evidence points to execution conditions, not a missing explanation.

options.text: Escalate the access issue through the approved support route and arrange supported practice.
options.feedback: Correct. Remove the practical barrier before using a realistic demonstration to check performance.

options.text: Mark Nia as unwilling.
options.feedback: The observation does not support that conclusion. Avoid attributing motive.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which is the strongest evidence of Ability for this scenario?

options.text: A correct description of the steps
Attendance at training
Completing an accurate handoff in a realistic practice ticket

knowledgeCheck.rationale: A realistic demonstration supplies direct performance evidence. Description and attendance alone do not.

lesson_activities.title: Support the behavior after launch

activity.prompt: Correct queue use falls after supervisors accept email again. Which plan is strongest?

options.text: Send one celebratory email and close the project.
options.feedback: Celebration alone leaves the mixed signal in place.

options.text: Review why email returned, align supervisor behavior and check handoff quality again next week.
options.feedback: Best choice. It examines the cause, changes the environment and checks whether the intended behavior persists.

options.text: Publish a lowest-performer list.
options.feedback: Public ranking can harm trust and does not address the conflicting workflow.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which observation most directly checks the intended outcome?

options.text: Number of launch messages sent
Percentage of sampled handoffs with an owner and usable next action
Number of slides in the tutorial

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The measure directly reflects the desired work behavior. The others measure communication or training inputs.

lesson_activities.title: Coach the next step

activity.prompt: Branch decision: after coverage is provided, Jordan completes the practice ticket accurately. What next?

options.text: Declare permanent adoption proven.
options.feedback: One successful attempt is useful evidence, but does not establish sustainment.

options.text: Check a later realistic handoff and discuss whether coverage remains workable.
options.feedback: Best choice. You have performance evidence; now test whether the support and behavior continue under realistic conditions.

options.text: Insist on repeating training anyway.
options.feedback: More of the same training is not supported by the current evidence. Revisit it if a knowledge gap appears.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which plan is most complete?

options.text: “Jordan needs a better attitude.”
“Send everyone the slides.”
“Agree coverage, observe an accurate handoff tomorrow, and review busy-shift use on Friday.”

knowledgeCheck.rationale: It names support, observable evidence and review timing. A full plan also states the target behavior explicitly.

assessment.instructions: Select one answer per question. Pass with at least 6 of 7 correct (85.7%, the first attainable score at or above 80%). Review explanations and retry as needed. This practice result is not a Prosci certification or validated change-readiness assessment.

questions.prompt: Sam asks, “What problem is the new process meant to solve?” Which element is most directly implicated?

options.text: Awareness
Ability
Reinforcement

questions.rationale: The question asks about the reason for change.

questions.prompt: Leila understands the reason but worries about a real loss of flexibility. Best first response?

options.text: Repeat the launch slogan
Ask about the impact and explore the concern honestly
Assume she does not understand the tutorial

questions.rationale: Listen to the participation concern and verify the facts. More procedural instruction does not address the stated issue.

questions.prompt: Omar wants to use the queue but does not know how to reassign a ticket. Most appropriate support?

options.text: Role-specific instruction with a worked example and check
Public recognition for adoption
A reminder of the project name

questions.rationale: The stated gap is procedural knowledge; instruction and a check target it.

questions.prompt: A colleague explains the steps accurately but an inaccessible control prevents completion. Best response?

options.text: Label the colleague unwilling
Ignore the issue because training is complete
Address the accessibility barrier and provide supported practice

questions.rationale: The barrier is in performing the task under available conditions. Knowledge alone cannot remove it.

questions.prompt: A month after successful use, the team returns to old habits because leaders accept both processes inconsistently. Best next action?

options.text: Align expectations, examine friction and check the new behavior again
Send a course-completion certificate
Assume initial knowledge has disappeared

questions.rationale: This responds to inconsistent reinforcement while checking for other causes.

questions.prompt: Which plan provides the clearest follow-through?

options.text: Improve adoption soon
Check morale sometime
Arrange coverage, observe one complete handoff tomorrow and review busy-shift use Friday

questions.rationale: It specifies support, evidence and timing; connect it to the defined handoff behavior.

questions.prompt: A learner says, “Everyone finished training, so the change has succeeded.” Best evaluation?

options.text: True: completion proves sustained performance
Incomplete: observe real behavior and whether it continues, and ask about remaining barriers
False: training never helps

questions.rationale: Completion is an input or learning milestone. Successful work and sustainment need additional evidence.

objectives.text: Given a simplified income statement, calculate EBIT and EBITDA and reconcile both to net income without double-counting.
Classify proposed adjustments as standard EBITDA components or additional adjustments in a supplied case.
Select and explain two reasons EBITDA can differ from operating cash flow or cash available for spending.
Evaluate a management claim and select an evidence-based response that uses the reconciliation and cash-flow information.

lesson_activities.title: Start with the question

activity.prompt: Which response best addresses the colleague’s cash claim?

options.text: The extra $96,000 must be cash in the bank.
options.feedback: Adding expenses back changes a metric; it does not create a cash receipt.

options.text: First trace the earnings adjustments, then inspect cash flows and obligations.
options.feedback: Best choice. The bridge explains the metric, while cash information supports a spending decision.

options.text: EBITDA is meaningless, so ignore it.
options.feedback: Too broad. A limited measure can be useful if its purpose and limitations are clear.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which question can an EBITDA bridge answer directly?

options.text: How much cash can be distributed?
How do interest, income tax and D&A explain the difference from net income?
Will customers pay on time?

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The bridge explains selected earnings adjustments; it does not show payment timing or distributable cash.

lesson_activities.title: Build the bridge in two directions

activity.prompt: A second synthetic quarter has net income 50, interest expense 12, income-tax expense 18 and D&A 25, all in USD thousands. What is EBITDA?

options.feedback: 80 is EBIT: 50 + 12 + 18. D&A still needs to be added.
Correct: 50 + 12 + 18 + 25 = 105. Reverse the bridge to confirm.
D&A has been added twice. Start at 50 and use each adjustment once.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Northstar’s EBIT is 140 and D&A is 40. What is EBITDA (USD thousands)?
knowledgeCheck.rationale: EBITDA = 140 + 40 = 180. Interest and tax have already been excluded from EBIT.

lesson_activities.title: Check the add-backs

activity.prompt: The draft adds a recurring software subscription of 6 to Northstar’s standard EBITDA of 180. What do you do?

options.text: Accept EBITDA of 186 because software is useful.
options.feedback: Usefulness does not make an operating expense an EBITDA add-back.

options.text: Keep standard EBITDA at 180 and ask for the basis of any separately labeled extra adjustment.
options.feedback: Correct. It is outside the basic components. Assess any adjusted measure critically rather than automatically accepting it.

options.text: Subtract the subscription from 180 again.
options.feedback: The subscription was already expensed in the starting earnings. Subtracting it again would double-count.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Net income is 20, interest expense 4, income-tax benefit 3 and D&A 9. EBITDA is:
knowledgeCheck.rationale: 20 + 4 − 3 + 9 = 30. The tax benefit is removed with a negative adjustment.

lesson_activities.title: Profit measures are not cash balances

activity.prompt: The manager says, “EBITDA is 180, so the 90 machine purchase is easily funded.” Choose your next step.

options.text: Approve from EBITDA alone.
options.feedback: The claim ignores payment timing and obligations.

options.text: Ask for current cash, cash forecast, capital spending and debt obligations before deciding.
options.feedback: Best response. This is the evidence needed to assess funding; EBITDA alone cannot establish it.

options.text: Say the company is insolvent because the example has −16 after capital spending.
options.feedback: A single simplified period does not establish insolvency. Financing and starting cash are still unknown.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which can reduce operating cash flow without reducing current-period EBITDA by the same amount?

options.text: Collecting all invoices immediately
A rise in unpaid customer invoices, all else equal
Adding back depreciation on a worksheet

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Accrual revenue can be recorded before collection. More cash tied up in receivables can reduce operating cash flow relative to earnings.

lesson_activities.title: Challenge a claim with useful evidence

activity.prompt: What happens next in the scenario?

options.text: You request a consistent bridge and a cash forecast.
options.feedback: The analyst finds that the comparable change is smaller. The cash forecast identifies a funding question for the finance team. You have improved the decision without overclaiming.

options.text: You repeat the 20% headline.
options.feedback: The meeting proceeds using an inconsistent comparison, and the supplier payment risk remains unexamined. Return to the bridge.

options.text: You remove every noncash expense from the company’s records.
options.feedback: A management measure does not authorize changing accounting records. Keep the records and review the analytical adjustments.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Two companies report different Adjusted EBITDA definitions. What is the strongest comparison approach?

options.text: Compare headline amounts without adjustments
Assume the higher amount means more cash
Inspect reconciliations and establish a consistent basis where possible

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Different exclusions can create an apparent performance gap. Read the bridges and retain the limits of comparability.

assessment.instructions: Select one answer per question. Earn at least 6 of 7 correct (85.7%, the first attainable score at or above 80%). Review rationales and retry after revisiting the relevant lessons. Completion is a portfolio practice result, not professional certification.

questions.prompt: Synthetic company: net income 72, interest expense 18, income-tax expense 30, depreciation 25, amortization 5 (USD thousands). What is EBITDA?
EBIT is 90. Depreciation is 12 and amortization 8. What is EBITDA?
questions.rationale: 90 + 12 + 8 = 110; do not add interest or tax again.

questions.prompt: Which proposed standard EBITDA add-back is incorrect?

options.text: Depreciation already included in cost of sales, counted once
Amortization already deducted in net income
The full cash purchase price of a new machine

questions.rationale: A capital purchase is not the same as the period’s depreciation expense.

questions.prompt: Net income 40 includes an income-tax benefit of 6. Interest expense is 4 and D&A is 10. EBITDA equals:
questions.rationale: 40 + 4 − 6 + 10 = 48. A benefit is removed by subtracting it.

questions.prompt: EBITDA is positive but many customers have not paid and equipment replacement is due. Which conclusion is supported?

options.text: There must be enough cash for replacement
Cash availability needs separate analysis
The unpaid invoices must be removed from revenue

questions.rationale: Receivable timing and capital expenditures matter to cash; EBITDA alone cannot settle the funding question.

questions.prompt: An analyst removes recurring software fees in addition to interest, tax and D&A. What should you do?

options.text: Accept the amount as standard EBITDA
Treat it as an extra adjustment, scrutinize the rationale and require a distinct measure label
Add the fees back a second time

questions.rationale: The exclusion goes beyond standard EBITDA. Labeling does not by itself make the adjustment appropriate.

questions.prompt: A slide reports “EBITDA increased, therefore next month’s loan principal payment is covered.” Your best response is:

options.text: Agree because principal is included in EBITDA
Check the earnings reconciliation, available cash and cash forecast including debt payments
Subtract amortization once more to prove coverage

questions.rationale: The claim jumps from an earnings metric to liquidity. Principal and cash timing require additional evidence.

course_analysis.performance_problem: a fictional service team completes mandatory training but continues to send incomplete handoffs.

Given a rollout case, distinguish a knowledge or skill gap from a tool, time, or permission barrier.
Select practice and feedback that address a stated handoff performance criterion.
Choose a transfer-support and evaluation plan that measures work performance without claiming that completion proves impact.

lesson_activities.title: 1. Begin with the work, then test your assumptions

activity.prompt: A capable new supervisor asks for a step-by-step demonstration before practicing. What should you do?

options.text: Remove the demonstration because adults should direct themselves.
options.feedback: Self-direction is an assumption to investigate. Withholding needed support creates an unnecessary obstacle.

options.text: Offer a short demonstration, then supported practice and a choice of relevant cases.
options.feedback: Best response. This respects the learner’s request while preserving a chance to perform the task.

options.text: Replace all practice with a lecture.
options.feedback: A demonstration can help, but observing alone does not show whether the learner can complete the task.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which statement is the most defensible starting point?

options.text: All adults need the same amount of independence.
Adults never benefit from explicit instruction.
Investigate learners’ readiness and experience before deciding how much guidance to provide.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Design decisions should follow evidence about this audience and task, rather than a rule based only on age.

lesson_activities.title: 2. Use experience without preserving errors

activity.prompt: An experienced agent’s demonstration reveals an outdated shortcut. Choose the strongest response.

options.text: Use contrasting old/new examples, explain the consequence, and let the agent retry.
options.feedback: Best response. It uses existing knowledge as a starting point and makes the changed requirement visible.

options.text: Tell the agent that past experience is irrelevant.
options.feedback: Discarding all experience loses valid knowledge and gives no precise correction.

options.text: Approve the shortcut because the agent has more experience.
options.feedback: Experience is valuable, but the shortcut still needs checking against the current process.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which feedback best addresses the actual error?

options.text: Try harder next time.
Your summary is clear; put the next owner in the Owner field so routing can use it.
You are an expert, so your answer is acceptable.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Specific feedback identifies what was successful, what must change, and why the correction matters.

lesson_activities.title: 3. Offer relevant choices and the support to succeed

activity.prompt: You have novices and experienced agents in one session. Which plan best balances choice and common expectations?

options.text: Let experienced staff skip verification based on their confidence.
options.feedback: Confidence alone does not establish performance with the changed process.

options.text: Make every learner read every explanation twice.
options.feedback: Uniform repetition ignores what learners already can do.

options.text: Offer optional scaffolds and relevant case choices, with the same required performance check.
options.feedback: Best response. Support can vary while the required standard stays clear.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Why provide a text alternative to a demonstration?

options.text: To support access and let learners revisit task details.
To assign permanent learning-style labels.
To eliminate the need for practice.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: A text alternative supports accessibility and flexible use. It does not diagnose a learning style or replace performance practice.

lesson_activities.title: 4. Make practice resemble the decision

activity.prompt: The objective is to route handoffs using a rule card. Which practice is best aligned?

options.text: Memorize the date the form was launched.
options.feedback: The launch date does not test the routing decision.

options.text: Choose owners for realistic cases using the rule card, receive explanations, and retry.
options.feedback: Best response. This practices the target decision under realistic reference conditions.

options.text: Watch a celebratory rollout video without making a decision.
options.feedback: The video may communicate a change, but it does not provide routing practice.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: A learner picks the wrong owner. What is the most useful immediate response?

options.text: Display only a red cross.
End the course.
Explain the relevant routing rule and offer a new attempt.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The learner needs actionable information and an opportunity to use it.

lesson_activities.title: 5. Plan transfer and measure what changed

activity.prompt: Agents pass practice but cannot open the owner list in production. What should the rollout lead prioritize?

options.text: Assign a longer repeat course to everyone.
options.feedback: Repeated instruction does not resolve a permission barrier.

options.text: Report completion as proof of successful adoption.
options.feedback: Completion does not demonstrate that the production workflow is usable.

options.text: Have the system owner resolve access and verify agents can use the list.
options.feedback: Best response. Resolve the enabling condition, then check actual performance.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which evidence most directly indicates the target behavior?

options.text: A sample of actual handoffs contains the required summary, owner, and next action.
Everyone viewed the opening slide.
The course has attractive colors.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The target behavior is a complete handoff. Other measures can inform implementation or experience, but they do not establish that behavior.

questions.prompt: A manager says every adult prefers completely independent learning. What is the best response?

options.text: Build an unguided course for everyone.
Check this group’s prior knowledge and support needs before choosing guidance.
Remove all learner choice.

questions.rationale: Andragogy provides assumptions to investigate; age alone does not determine the right support.

questions.prompt: The new form reads its Owner field, while a veteran puts the owner only in notes. Choose the most useful intervention.

options.text: Compare the two workflows and practice entering the owner in the correct field.
Ask the veteran to repeat the old workflow faster.
Assume the veteran is unwilling to learn.

questions.rationale: A contrast and retry address the specific outdated mental model without inventing a motivation problem.

questions.prompt: Which choice preserves a common performance standard?

options.text: Allow confident users to skip all checks.
Give every person an unrelated topic.
Offer two relevant case contexts with the same required handoff fields.

questions.rationale: Context can vary while required behavior and assessment criteria remain consistent.

questions.prompt: A designer offers text and demonstration versions. Which explanation is appropriate?

options.text: Each learner belongs permanently to one sensory learning type.
Different formats can support access and revisiting task details.
Text is always superior for every task.

questions.rationale: Choose formats for accessibility and task demands, not fixed learning-style categories.

questions.prompt: Which assessment is closest to an objective about selecting a next owner?

options.text: Select an owner for a new case using the work rule card.
Recall the launch date.
Rate the animation quality.

questions.rationale: A case decision samples the required performance; the other options measure unrelated knowledge or experience.

questions.prompt: An agent understands the procedure but lacks system permissions. What is the primary next action?

options.text: Repeat the definitions quiz.
Label the agent resistant.
Resolve access with the system owner and verify the workflow.

questions.rationale: The barrier is an enabling condition, not evidence of a knowledge deficit.

questions.prompt: Which feedback best supports correction?

options.text: Wrong.
The issue summary is clear; the next action is missing, so add what the receiving agent should do.
You need a better attitude.

questions.rationale: The feedback names a successful element and a specific correction tied to the criterion.

questions.prompt: After training, handoff quality improves while the form is also redesigned. What can you conclude?

options.text: Performance improved in the observed sample; more evidence is needed to isolate causes.
Training alone caused the entire improvement.
Completion statistics prove every agent is proficient.

questions.rationale: An observed change is useful evidence, but the concurrent form change prevents a simple causal attribution.

lesson_activities.title: 1. Read the revised taxonomy accurately

activity.prompt: A stakeholder asks you to label a routine record-entry task “Create” because it sounds more advanced. What should you do?

options.text: Use Create on every objective.
options.feedback: The label would overstate what the task requires.

options.text: Classify the actual cognitive work; executing a specified entry procedure is generally Apply.
options.feedback: Best response. Fit the category to the required action and context.

options.text: Remove all objectives.
options.feedback: Objectives are still useful for clarifying the intended performance.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which list belongs to the 2001 revised cognitive taxonomy?

options.text: Knowledge, Comprehension, Application, Analysis, Synthesis, Evaluation.
Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create.
Recall, Attend, Repeat, Reward, Pass, Certify.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The revised list uses these six process categories; the first option uses original taxonomy labels.

lesson_activities.title: 2. Classify the task, not just its verb

activity.prompt: A quiz says “Analyze this term” but asks learners to select its memorized definition. How should you review it?

options.text: Call it Analyze because the prompt uses that word.
options.feedback: The word does not create analytical demand.

options.text: Call every multiple-choice item Remember.
options.feedback: The response format alone does not determine cognitive demand; a case-based item can require reasoning.

options.text: Classify the actual demand as recognition of a definition and revise if analysis is required.
options.feedback: Best response. Examine the work required, then address any mismatch.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: A learner judges two plans against an explicit quality rubric. Which category best describes that task?

options.text: Evaluate.
Remember.
Apply only because all work involves an action.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Judgment against stated criteria is characteristic of Evaluate.

lesson_activities.title: 3. Turn an intention into an observable objective

activity.prompt: Which objective is most ready to guide a case-based assessment?

options.text: Appreciate excellent customer service.
options.feedback: The intention needs observable evidence and clearer scope.

options.text: Given the rule card and four ticket cases, assign priorities with at least three correct.
options.feedback: Best response. Behavior, conditions, and criterion are explicit.

options.text: Learn everything about ticketing quickly.
options.feedback: This does not define the expected behavior or acceptable standard.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: In “Given a rule card, classify four tickets with three correct,” what is the condition?

options.text: Three correct.
Classify.
Given a rule card.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The rule card is part of the conditions; classify is the behavior and three correct is the criterion.

lesson_activities.title: 4. Align objective, practice, and evidence

activity.prompt: Your objective requires producing a new onboarding plan. The test asks learners to pick the best of three finished plans. What is the best revision?

options.text: Keep the test and claim it proves creation.
options.feedback: Selection does not demonstrate that the learner can independently produce a plan.

options.text: Add more definitions to the same test.
options.feedback: More recall items do not supply the missing production evidence.

options.text: Ask learners to produce a plan and assess it against explicit criteria; retain plan comparisons as practice.
options.feedback: Best response. The assessment now elicits the performance named by the objective.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which trio is best aligned to applying a routing procedure?

options.text: Objective: route cases; practice: route worked and new cases; assessment: route another case using the procedure.
Objective: route cases; practice: watch a branding video; assessment: name the logo color.
Objective: create a procedure; practice: memorize queue names; assessment: recall one name.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The first trio consistently elicits and supports the required routing performance.

lesson_activities.title: 5. Review a small curriculum as an L&D partner

activity.prompt: A sponsor says an 80% terminology score proves readiness to triage unfamiliar cases. What should you recommend?

options.text: Add realistic triage evidence before making the readiness claim.
options.feedback: Best response. Readiness for case decisions needs evidence of those decisions.

options.text: Accept the claim because the score is high.
options.feedback: A high score on a different task does not establish the required performance.

options.text: Make the terminology questions longer.
options.feedback: Length does not repair the mismatch in cognitive demand.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: What should a curriculum review prioritize?

options.text: Using Create in every objective.
Matching the required performance with practice and assessment evidence.
Making every lesson equally long regardless of purpose.

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The review should establish a defensible relationship between what is promised, practiced, and assessed.

questions.prompt: Which category follows Evaluate in the revised taxonomy’s usual sequence?

options.text: Synthesis.
Create.
Comprehension.

questions.rationale: The revised sequence ends with Evaluate and Create; Synthesis and Comprehension are original labels.

questions.prompt: A learner executes a supplied routing procedure on a ticket. What category best fits?

options.text: Apply.
Create.
Remember only.

questions.rationale: Using the supplied procedure is Apply; no new procedure is being produced.

questions.prompt: A prompt says “Evaluate” but asks only for a memorized queue name. What should the reviewer conclude?

options.text: The verb establishes Evaluate.
All queue tasks are Create.
The actual demand is factual recall or recognition, despite the label.

questions.rationale: Classification follows the cognitive work required, not a decorative verb.

questions.prompt: Which objective best specifies observable performance?

options.text: Understand reporting.
Given a report and a checklist, identify every missing required section.
Become a strong professional.

questions.rationale: This objective names a behavior, a condition, and a criterion.

questions.prompt: A learner distinguishes common causes from unrelated details across several reports. Which category best fits?

options.text: Analyze.
Remember.
Create, because there are several reports.

questions.rationale: Examining parts and their relationships is Analyze; quantity alone does not make a task Create.

questions.prompt: An objective requires designing a new process. Which evidence most directly supports it?

options.text: A terminology score.
A satisfaction rating.
A learner-produced process assessed against explicit criteria.

questions.rationale: Creation requires evidence of the produced artifact, not merely recognition or satisfaction.

questions.prompt: Staff must judge escalation proposals against impact, staffing, and response-time criteria. Which complete objective–practice–assessment plan best fits?

options.text: Objective: judge proposals against the three criteria. Practice: memorize queue names. Assessment: recall the definition of escalation.

Objective: judge proposals against the three criteria. Practice: compare proposals using those criteria and receive feedback. Assessment: select and justify the strongest judgment of a new proposal using the same criteria.
Objective: produce a new escalation workflow. Practice: watch a welcome video. Assessment: rate satisfaction with the video.

questions.rationale: The second plan aligns the required judgment, criterion-based practice, and evidence from a new proposal. The first substitutes recall for judgment; the third promises creation but assesses satisfaction.

questions.prompt: A learner recognizes when their own understanding is weak and selects a checking strategy. Which knowledge dimension is most directly involved?

options.text: Metacognitive.
Factual only.
A seventh cognitive-process category called Confidence.

questions.rationale: Metacognitive knowledge concerns awareness and regulation of one’s own thinking; it is a knowledge dimension, not a seventh process category.

lesson_activities.title: Define the reader’s job and find the home

activity.prompt: You find an existing current runbook with the same scope. What should you do?

options.text: Create an unrelated copy with a similar title.
options.feedback: Competing pages make it harder to identify the authoritative instructions.

options.text: Review and update the canonical page through its ownership process.
options.feedback: Correct. Preserve one clear source when its scope still fits.

options.text: Delete it without reading.
options.feedback: You have not established that it should be removed or that you may delete it.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Why use a page rather than a live doc for this sample?

options.text: The team wants a deliberate publishing checkpoint
Live docs cannot contain text
Pages automatically prove approval

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The content choice supports the requested workflow; publishing does not itself prove review or approval.

lesson_activities.title: Write a procedure with observable decisions

activity.prompt: Which instruction best replaces “Ask Morgan”?

options.text: Ask whoever is around.
options.feedback: The owner and evidence requirements remain unclear.

options.text: At the stated stop condition, contact the named support role with job ID, status, elapsed time, and non-sensitive error code.
options.feedback: Correct. The reader knows when to stop, where to go, and what evidence to provide.

options.text: Keep rerunning until it works.
options.feedback: Repeated jobs may create additional problems and ignore the stop condition.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: The demo job is Processing at 12 minutes. What does the sample procedure require?

options.text: Restart repeatedly
Use the stated escalation route with the specified evidence
Wait indefinitely

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The invented 10-minute threshold has been exceeded; follow the documented stop condition.

lesson_activities.title: Check access before distributing the link

activity.prompt: An analyst cannot open the page because its parent is restricted. What next?

options.text: Make the page public.
options.feedback: That broadens access without establishing that public exposure is appropriate.

options.text: Send the same link again.
options.feedback: A repeated URL cannot resolve a permission boundary.

options.text: Have the authorized owner inspect the location and access constraints, then verify with an intended reader.
options.feedback: Correct. Resolve the actual access issue through the approved process.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Does sending a page link guarantee the recipient can read it?

options.text: Yes
Only if its title is descriptive
No; their effective access still matters

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Links point to content; they do not automatically grant all required permissions.

lesson_activities.title: Review, publish, and test the reader experience

activity.prompt: Your edit is saved, but the reader sees the old instructions. What should you check first?

options.text: Whether the intended page changes have been published or updated.
options.feedback: Correct. Saving draft changes and publishing the reader-facing version are different steps.

options.text: Whether the reader can lend you their password.
options.feedback: Never request another person’s credentials.

options.text: Whether the title needs more exclamation marks.
options.feedback: That does not address which version is visible.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which review most directly tests usability?

options.text: Counting how many headings exist
Asking a new reader to choose actions from realistic cases using only the draft
Having the author say the page looks good

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Observed reader performance reveals ambiguity that an author may overlook.

lesson_activities.title: Maintain the canonical answer

activity.prompt: The threshold changes to 15 minutes. Which update plan is best?

options.text: Change only the page title.
options.feedback: The actual decision instructions would remain stale.

options.text: Update all affected steps and examples, retest the decision cases, then publish the reviewed change.
options.feedback: Correct. Consistent content and renewed testing support safe reuse.

options.text: Leave 10 and 15 in different sections so readers can choose.
options.feedback: Contradictory instructions force the reader to guess.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: What should trigger a runbook review before its scheduled date?

options.text: An underlying workflow change
A colleague’s preference for another font
Nothing; only the calendar matters

knowledgeCheck.rationale: A material process change can make the instructions wrong immediately.

questions.prompt: A current page already covers the same procedure. What is the strongest approach?

options.text: Create three duplicates
Maintain the canonical page through its owner
Delete the existing page immediately

questions.rationale: A clear authoritative destination reduces contradictory guidance.

questions.prompt: Which step is most usable?

options.text: Check stuff
Do the usual fix
Match the job ID, read the status, and apply the stated decision rule

questions.rationale: It provides an action, observation, and decision basis.

questions.prompt: In the original sample rule, Processing has lasted 12 minutes. What should the learner do?

options.text: Use the specified escalation route
Rerun repeatedly
Download any file available

questions.rationale: The sample threshold is 10 minutes and the prescribed stop condition is met.

questions.prompt: The page sits under a restricted parent. What should happen before distribution?

options.text: Assume sharing the URL grants access
Verify intended-reader access and resolve constraints through the authorized owner
Make everything public

questions.rationale: Access must be checked in its actual hierarchy and policy context.

questions.prompt: What proves the reader-facing page includes your revision?

options.text: A saved draft exists
You typed the change
The change was published and verified in the rendered reader view

questions.rationale: Publication and verification establish what readers can actually see.

questions.prompt: The process changes next week, before the review date. What is appropriate?

options.text: Wait for the date regardless
Review and update affected instructions now through the owner
Keep both contradictory procedures

questions.rationale: Process changes are meaningful review triggers independent of the calendar.

analysis.needsValidation: Before workplace deployment, interview a process owner and two target learners, confirm common errors, access roles, local vocabulary, and policy requirements.

design.strategy: Task-centered worked example followed by progressively independent decision practice. Feedback explains consequences, not just correctness.
design.mastery: 80% of six equally weighted questions requires at least five correct (83.3%). A portfolio knowledge check is not authorization to perform production work.
design.durationEstimate: Estimated 28 minutes including a three-minute learner-authored task; not pilot-tested. Learner pace varies.

development.artifact: Five original text-led lessons, five decision scenarios with option-specific feedback, five formative checks, six scored questions with rationales, and a concise job aid.
development.accessibility: Use semantic headings, keyboard-operable choices, visible focus, text feedback, and readable contrast in the delivery player. Do not rely on color or timing alone. Test the implemented player with keyboard and screen reader before release.
development.sourcePolicy: Official product docs establish limited platform facts. Synthetic policies, examples, case decisions, and instructional writing are original. No vendor screenshots, course assets, client data, or claimed client results are included.

implementation.launchChecks: Validate JSON and option keys; test choice feedback, score calculation, retry, progress navigation, links, mobile readability, and accessibility in the final player. A content file alone does not establish runtime behavior.
implementation.facilitatorOption: Ask learners to explain the evidence behind one incorrect choice and identify the equivalent role or process in their own organization without sharing confidential details.

evaluation.formative: Track scenario misconceptions during a pilot; ask learners to restate the next action in their own words. Use feedback for revision, not ranking.

lesson_activities.title: Search before creating

activity.prompt: HBR-84 has the same dataset, build, and missing rows. What is the best next step?

options.text: Create a new item immediately.
options.feedback: This risks duplicate work before checking the existing record.

options.text: Inspect HBR-84 and add relevant evidence if it is the same defect.
options.feedback: Correct. Compare behavior and context, then maintain a coherent record.

options.text: Delete HBR-71.
options.feedback: A different PDF defect can remain valid; similarity is not deletion authority.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which evidence most strongly suggests a duplicate?

options.text: The same word export
Matching behavior, context, and affected build
The oldest creation date

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Comparable symptoms and conditions are stronger evidence than a shared keyword.

lesson_activities.title: Write a record another person can reproduce

activity.prompt: Which evidence should accompany the sample defect?

options.text: A full production customer export.
options.feedback: That can disclose unnecessary private data.

options.text: A synthetic before/after code and reproduction steps.
options.feedback: Correct. It demonstrates the behavior with minimal, safe evidence.

options.text: Only the phrase export broken.
options.feedback: The team still lacks a reproducible problem definition.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Why inspect the raw CSV rather than only a spreadsheet cell?

options.text: To distinguish source output from display formatting
To make the ticket longer
To avoid describing the environment

knowledgeCheck.rationale: A spreadsheet may format identifiers differently; the raw output isolates the observed behavior.

lesson_activities.title: Make acceptance and ownership explicit

activity.prompt: Which acceptance criterion is testable?

options.text: The export should be better.
options.feedback: Better is subjective and gives no pass/fail test.

options.text: Export DEMO-7 and verify raw CSV preserves 00127 and 00008 exactly.
options.feedback: Correct. A tester can observe the output and make a repeatable decision.

options.text: Finish this as soon as possible.
options.feedback: That expresses urgency, not a verification criterion.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Who should set priority when local policy reserves it for triage?

options.text: Any person who wants faster service
The authorized triager using documented impact and urgency
Nobody; every item must be highest priority

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Follow the agreed role boundary and provide evidence instead of silently overriding it.

lesson_activities.title: Represent progress and blockers honestly

activity.prompt: Code is complete, but acceptance checks have not run. What is the best handoff?

options.text: Mark Done to improve the board.
options.feedback: The stated completion evidence is missing.

options.text: Use the approved test-ready transition with build and test instructions.
options.feedback: Correct. The state and handoff reflect actual progress.

options.text: Delete the acceptance criteria.
options.feedback: That removes the standard for completion rather than meeting it.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: A transition is unavailable. What should a contributor do?

options.text: Bypass it using another account
Consult the configured process or authorized administrator
Assume Jira is broken and duplicate the item

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Transitions depend on workflow configuration and permissions.

lesson_activities.title: Close with evidence, reopen with specificity

activity.prompt: The second acceptance case still fails. Choose your update.

options.text: All fixed; the main example passed.
options.feedback: That hides a known failure.

options.text: Leave no comment and wait.
options.feedback: The next owner will not know what failed or why.

options.text: Record the failing case and return it through the approved workflow.
options.feedback: Correct. Specific evidence supports an actionable continuation.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: What supports completion in this sample?

options.text: Coding ended
Every stated acceptance check and required review passed
The ticket has been open for a week

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Completion is evidence-based, not based only on effort or age.

questions.prompt: Two reports mention export. What determines whether you should combine them?

options.text: Matching underlying behavior and context
Their titles have the same length
Both requesters are impatient

questions.rationale: Compare reproducible behavior, not just wording.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest defect title?

options.text: Broken again
CSV export removes leading zeros from product codes
Urgent!!!

questions.rationale: The title identifies the affected function and observable defect.

questions.prompt: Which phrase is a hypothesis rather than an observation?

options.text: Raw CSV shows 127
Source code is 00127
The serializer must be defective

questions.rationale: The proposed cause is not established by the output alone.

questions.prompt: Which acceptance criterion enables a repeatable check?

options.text: Looks right
Preserve 00127 exactly in raw CSV for DEMO-7
Make the user happy

questions.rationale: It specifies the fixture, output, and expected value.

questions.prompt: The fix awaits testing. Which sample state is appropriate when its prerequisites are met?

options.text: Done
Archived
Ready for Test

questions.rationale: The sample separates implementation from verification; use the local equivalent.

questions.prompt: Five of six required checks pass. What next?

options.text: Report the failed check and continue through the agreed workflow
Mark Done because most checks pass
Remove the last check

questions.rationale: A known unmet criterion needs an explicit resolution, not silent closure.

course_analysis.title: SAP Fieldglass: Review Time Sheets with Confidence
course_analysis.learner_segment: New buyer-side contingent-workforce supervisors who approve submitted time sheets.
course_analysis.performance_problem: approving the weekly total without checking daily evidence can delay correction and invoicing.

objectives.text: Select the correct submitted time sheet using worker, assignment, and period identifiers.
Reconcile a submitted standard time sheet against daily evidence and a supplied coding rule.
Choose approval, rejection, or escalation and write an actionable reason.
Verify the workflow outcome and recognize when an invoiced record needs a revision process.

lesson_activities.title: Start with the right record

activity.prompt: Which record should you open for this request?

options.text: TS-099 because the name and week match.
options.feedback: The assignment differs. Name and period alone do not establish the correct record.

options.text: TS-104 because worker, assignment, and week match.
options.feedback: Correct. You have matched all three identifiers before reviewing the details.

options.text: Whichever record appears first.
options.feedback: Sorting is not evidence of identity or approval authority.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which combination identifies this review target?

options.text: Worker name only
Weekly total and supplier
Worker, assignment, and period

knowledgeCheck.rationale: The review request identifies all three. Verify status and authority next.

lesson_activities.title: Reconcile daily detail, not only totals

activity.prompt: The weekly total is corrected to 38, but Wednesday still shows 8 DEL. What now?

options.text: Approve because the weekly total matches.
options.feedback: The total now matches, but coding still conflicts with the evidence.

options.text: Request Wednesday’s 6 DEL plus 2 TRN correction.
options.feedback: Correct. Accuracy includes allocation as well as total hours.

options.text: Change all days to TRN.
options.feedback: That replaces one error with several unsupported entries.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: What is the verified coding breakdown?

options.text: 38 DEL, 0 TRN
36 DEL, 2 TRN
40 DEL, 2 TRN

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday: 24 DEL; Wednesday and Friday: 12 DEL; Wednesday training: 2 TRN.

lesson_activities.title: Choose the action and explain the correction

activity.prompt: Choose the most useful rejection reason.

options.text: Wrong. Fix it.
options.feedback: Too vague: the submitter cannot tell which dates or codes to examine.

options.text: You exaggerated your hours.
options.feedback: This asserts motive that the evidence does not establish.

options.text: Check Wednesday’s DEL/TRN split and Friday’s 6 verified hours; correct and resubmit for 38 total.
options.feedback: Correct. It identifies the discrepancies and next action without blame.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Two reliable source records disagree about Friday. What is the best next step?

options.text: Approve the larger amount
Clarify the discrepancy through the approved contact before deciding
Reject with an accusation

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Unresolved evidence requires clarification. Do not manufacture a correct value.

lesson_activities.title: Review the resubmission and verify the outcome

activity.prompt: After your approval, the screen indicates another approval stage. What do you report?

options.text: Payment is complete.
options.feedback: Approval is not proof of payment.

options.text: My review is complete; the record remains in the next approval stage.
options.feedback: Correct. The report distinguishes your action from the wider process.

options.text: The application failed because the status is not final.
options.feedback: A configured approval route may legitimately contain multiple stages.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: What should you do after submitting an approval?

options.text: Verify the displayed status or history
Immediately approve every remaining sheet
Tell the supplier payment has arrived

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Verify the outcome and communicate only the state supported by the record.

lesson_activities.title: Handle the exception you cannot simply undo

activity.prompt: TS-088 is already invoiced. Which response is safest?

options.text: Delete the original record and start over.
options.feedback: That bypasses the approved correction and audit process.

options.text: Create another normal sheet with negative hours.
options.feedback: An improvised offset may cause additional errors.

options.text: Provide the discrepancy evidence to the authorized owner for the revision process.
options.feedback: Correct. Use the eligible, configured correction route rather than improvising.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which detail is essential in a revision handoff?

options.text: A guess about why the worker erred
Affected record, line, verified difference, and evidence
Only the worker’s first name

knowledgeCheck.rationale: Specific record and evidence details let the authorized owner investigate without speculation.

questions.prompt: The right worker has two assignments in the same week. Which sheet do you review?

options.text: The newer sheet
The sheet matching the requested assignment and period
Both without checking

questions.rationale: Match the full review target; recency does not resolve assignment identity.

questions.prompt: Evidence is 8, 8, 8, 8, and 6 hours. What total should you expect?
questions.rationale: Four 8-hour days plus 6 equals 38.

questions.prompt: A total matches but 2 training hours are charged to delivery. What should happen under the sample policy?

options.text: Approve the total
Remove the training hours
Request the coding correction

questions.rationale: Correct allocation is required even when the total is right.

questions.prompt: Which correction note is actionable?

options.text: Bad submission
Please compare Friday with the verified 6-hour record, correct the current 8 hours, and resubmit
You always get this wrong

questions.rationale: It identifies date, discrepancy, evidence, and next action.

questions.prompt: An invoiced sheet has a confirmed error. What is the next route?

options.text: Authorized revised-time-sheet process
Delete it without review
Approve it again

questions.rationale: The normal rejection assumption no longer applies to an invoiced sheet.

questions.prompt: A successful supervisor approval proves what?

options.text: The worker has been paid
Every approval stage is finished
Your approval was recorded, subject to the displayed workflow state

questions.rationale: Payment and final routing are separate outcomes that need separate evidence.
